Rust's last_message_owner survives GroupEnd, contradicting SequenceDiagram.grouping where END replaces lastEventWithDeactivate with GroupingLeaf; three fresh group-reset cases fail and add a false 30px row.

Rust applies unrelated lifecycle types to self-message ownership, while AbstractMessage.addLifeEvent returns before recording them; the fresh self-message case adds a false 30px row.
An active semantic source moves source-cross half-arrow geometry by one activation half-width even though the inactive control passes.
Owner-preserving notes, group starts, dividers, and deep right-border cases expose stale independent depth or extent consumers.

Apply AbstractMessage's self-message participant filter before lifecycle types affect owner row allocation.
Replace spacing, note, external-width, activation-bar, and rendering depth reconstructions with projections from one normalized timeline.
Derive half-arrow source decorations from the exact live segment at the message ordinate, including active and nested sources.
Make divider and group extents consume the final shared external area rather than a pre-external canvas width.
Rebuild the immutable implementation, replay all preserved review6_ failures, and commission a new independent checker with additional fresh inputs.
